## The Gear-Only Matters If Your Photo Doesn’t Suck

A spirited debate has erupted on 4chan’s /gear/ board, crystallizing around a new unofficial community motto: "gear only matters if your photo doesn’t suck." This sentiment marks a cultural shift among enthusiasts, prioritizing compositional skill and subject matter over technical specifications. The thread, which has generated several iterations, argues that opinions from individuals who do not post their work are invalid by default. In this hierarchy, visual proof outweighs gear acquisition syndrome (GAS).

The discussion is highlighted by playful interactions, including a pun where one user types 'grate' instead of 'great,' reinforcing the idea that the community values the final output above all else. Beyond the philosophical debate, users are also dissecting specific hardware anomalies, such as a rumored camera body featuring a Fujifilm GFX front, a Nikon top plate, and a Sony back. These discussions collectively suggest a growing cynicism toward marketing hype, with hobbyists asserting that competence remains the primary driver of quality imagery.

## Analog Revival: First Film Cameras

The analog photography community on Newsblur is buzzing with excitement over new members acquiring their first film cameras. This trend highlights the enduring appeal of the medium’s learning curve and aesthetic. @SpiritedAssumption3 recently purchased a Canon Canonet 28 via eBay and is seeking advice on navigating indoor portraits and selecting film stocks like Kodak Gold 200. Meanwhile, @Whereishumhum- is testing an heirloom camera inherited from their grandfather, likely dating back to the 1990s.

Both users are exploring whether starting with film is a viable method for perfecting skills and capturing a specific emotional resonance compared to digital. The conversation underscores the technical challenges beginners face, particularly regarding manual controls, ISO variations, and fixed aperture modes. Despite these hurdles, the consensus is that film offers a unique tactile experience and a distinct aesthetic feel that continues to attract new practitioners to the darkroom arts.

## Audio Tech: Neve, Etude, and Terrifying Choirs

The audio engineering world is seeing significant developments in software and interactive gaming. Rupert Neve Designs has announced software plug-in versions of three of its most acclaimed hardware units: the Portico II Master Buss Processor, the 551 Inductor EQ, and the 542 Tape Emulator. This release allows producers to access the company’s signature analog warmth and character within digital audio workstations, bridging the gap between physical studio staples and digital flexibility.

On the gaming front, *Etude*, a new music title by developer Eiður, has launched on Steam. Supporting up to six simultaneous players on Windows and Mac, the game focuses on multiplayer improvisation using MIDI keyboards and live sequencers, emphasizing collaborative creation.

In a more niche release, The Crow Hill Company has introduced "CHILDREN'S CHOIR," an audio sample library described as offering "terrifying sounds from schoolkids." Promoted for its eerie and unsettling vocal characteristics, the product targets horror and dramatic audio production, appealing to sound designers looking for unique, high-quality organic textures.

## Computational Efficiency and Final Fantasy VII

In the tech sphere, a discussion on Bluesky centered on the computational efficiency of Large Language Models (LLMs) versus biological systems. @Grace clarified that while LLMs perform billions of computations to output a single token, these calculations are not redundant; results are reused for subsequent tokens. @Dr Keith Wilson contrasted this discrete, energy-intensive process with the real-time, low-energy operation of biological neural networks. Grace argued that the continuity in LLMs is a property of the outer loop, with gaps between forward passes being negligible for practical purposes.

Pop culture enthusiasts also revisited *Final Fantasy VII* in a humorous workplace analogy. A commenter named Comrade Lunagris pointed out the financial anxiety of a Sector 7 middle manager viewing unaffordable homes, noting that the ruthless executive Hojo likely wouldn’t take his wife and child. The thread captures the classic dynamic of financial stress balanced by family stability amidst the city’s extreme class divide.

## Quick Hits

*   **YWNBAW Reclaimed:** A petition on Bluesky seeks to redefine the acronym **YWNBAW** ("You Will Never Be A Witch") to include wizards ("You **Will** Never Be A Witch/Wizard"), broadening the inclusivity of the witchy aesthetic subculture.
*   **Mondsee Identified:** On 4chan’s /rpt/ thread, users successfully identified a photo of Mondsee, with context provided that the view was taken from a restaurant directly next to the highway.
*   **General Unsorted:** 207 items remained unclassified in the digest, reflecting the chaotic nature of the social media inbox.

I have a gut feeling that my first ever test roll is going to come out horrible but now getting more comfortable I’d love to know what advice you have for taking portraits and photos inside and what film stocks to use. So far I’ve been using Kodak gold 200 and I took a lot of photos outside but with my friends I’ve been mostly indoors and messing with the Aperture because it locks on the A mode.
